calls.reason: ETR finds cost-driven shifts to open-weight models, but 93% of their production users report growing proprietary usage. There is no evidence of broad abandonment, and the forecast has no deadline.
XenoSpectrum reports worsening OpenAI losses on a GAAP basis, while Yahoo reports rising Anthropic compute costs. Neither establishes the claimed comparable non-GAAP margin deterioration.

Anthropic's studies show both task limitations and successful improvements. They establish neither a general inability to train reliable task performance nor its alleged role in driving benchmark optimization.

Cloudera reports widespread workload redesign due to costs, while ETR finds most over-budget firms keep funding AI. Neither establishes broad spending cuts or costs exceeding every other organizational expense.

The IEA's illustrative fourfold comparison and IREN's 50 MW GPU site challenge the claimed range. But neither provides a matched comparison with social-media or streaming facilities sufficient to call the general claim.

The Next Web reports reduced allowances for new OpenAI Pro 200 subscribers, and BleepingComputer documents changed Claude allowances across paid plans. These support the ordinary reading that what subscriptions buy is unstable.
